Status

FinKore Core 2.0.4 stable.

Purpose

This document defines the portable Entity import boundary for observing an existing Financial Entity, preserving supplied business revision history, and recording explicit source identity mapping when import or migration uses an external identity. It does not define a master-data registry, persistence, deduplication, authorization, or concrete financial document formats.

Terminology

Entity Import is the operation that accepts a supplied existing Entity observation and returns a validated import observation.

Source Identity is an opaque identifier supplied by an external or legacy system. It does not replace stable FinKore Entity identity.

Entity Identity Mapping is explicit evidence that relates a Source Identity to the stable FinKore Entity identity preserved by import.

Expected Entity State, Expected Entity Revision, and Expected Entity Conflict Version are optional caller-supplied preconditions checked against the imported observation.

Requirements

  • ENTITY-IMPORT-001 - Entity Import MUST preserve the supplied stable FinKore Entity identity. It MUST NOT generate a replacement identity or substitute a Source Identity for stable Entity identity.
  • ENTITY-IMPORT-002 - Entity Import MUST validate the complete supplied Entity observation using the Entity identity, lifecycle, mutability, validation, and referenced Workflow requirements before returning an import observation. Every Structural Validation and Business Validation rule declared for the Entity's supplied current State applies to import in the same way that it applies to an already-observed Entity; import MUST NOT bypass a declared validator merely because no Mutation is being proposed.

    Research / Supports the rationale

    Observed input still needs the applicable business validation ↗

    Mohamed Nofel; Mahmoud Marzouk; Hany Elbardan; Reda Saleh; Aly Mogahed

    Declared structural/business validation applies to the complete supplied result, including import. The proposed sensor pipeline motivates that boundary without certifying fact truth, accounting recognition, IoT, blockchain or XBRL.

    Scope and limitations

    This transfer is reviewer inference, not a rule formulated by the authors for FinKore. A sensor’s inventory observation alone does not establish a sale. Cleaning data must not silently invent business facts.

    Research / Clarifies a boundary

    Successful import does not authenticate a complete historical record ↗

    László Szívós; István Orosz

    Validation preserves the supplied observation and history; empty supplied history is not historical completeness, and Workflow import creates no transition or Audit evidence. Legacy authentication/reconciliation remains separate.

    Scope and limitations

    A post-migration consistency check can find violated relations but is limited by the predicates and data it covers. Source authentication, omitted history and external reconciliation are separate application responsibilities.

    Legacy / Supports the rationale

    Validate supplied financial observations without confusing validity with factual truth ↗

    Elaine Richardson

    Import validates the complete supplied observation and must not bypass declared validators simply because no Mutation is proposed.

    Scope and limitations

    Product-specific names, address formats and numeric-field rules must be declared by a composing domain. The anecdote supplies no universal input grammar or guarantee that a validator detects fraud, missing facts, or all bad assumptions. FinKore validates declared conditions against supplied observations; it does not certify their real-world truth.

  • ENTITY-IMPORT-003 - When Entity Import supplies Source Identity, it MUST also supply explicit Entity Identity Mapping evidence that identifies the source system, source identity, mapped Entity type, mapped Entity identity, and mapping identity.
  • ENTITY-IMPORT-004 - Entity Identity Mapping evidence MUST be preserved as opaque caller-supplied values. An implementation MUST NOT parse source-system formats, infer tenancy, deduplicate entities, or look up a global registry from mapping content.
  • ENTITY-IMPORT-005 - Entity Identity Mapping MUST map to the same stable Entity type and Entity identity as the imported Entity observation.
  • ENTITY-IMPORT-006 - Entity Import MUST preserve supplied Current Entity Revision, Historical Entity Revisions, and Entity Conflict Version as distinct opaque values.

  • ENTITY-IMPORT-007 - Entity Import with an Expected Entity State, Expected Entity Revision, or Expected Entity Conflict Version that does not match the supplied observation MUST fail with FINKORE_ENTITY_STATE_CONFLICT.
    Evidence & context2 research notes · 1 practitioner account+

    These sources inform discussion of this rule. Their role and limits are stated separately; a citation is not certification or specialist sign-off. Notes from the same study are not independent confirmation.

    Research / Illustrates a risk

    Fast responses do not establish that the relevant facts are current ↗

    Ruth Octaviani P. Wermasubun; Linjte Kalangi; Heince R. N. Wokas

    Explicit dependencies and comparisons against supplied observations do not guarantee freshness of remote facts. The reported synchronization issue motivates a conditional application risk, not a Core age limit.

    Scope and limitations

    The source reports synchronization issues, not a measured stale-snapshot control failure. The financial scenario in the original finding is reviewer-created. Historical reports may intentionally use old observations.

    Research / Clarifies a boundary

    Snapshot coherence and freshness are separate properties ↗

    Dan R. K. Ports; Austin T. Clements; Irene Zhang; Samuel Madden; Barbara Liskov

    Explicit context and supplied-observation checks do not certify a coherent or sufficiently recent remote snapshot. The cache source distinguishes coherence from age; acceptable age and isolation remain composing-application choices.

    Scope and limitations

    These financial scenarios are reviewer inferences. A consistent snapshot can be appropriate within an application’s bound. TxCache does not remove the database’s anomalies or establish universal safe staleness for financial authorization.

    Legacy / Clarifies a boundary

    Batch dependencies expose a distinction between reproducible facts and fresh facts ↗

    Elaine Richardson

    Expected state/revision/conflict values are checked against the supplied observation; passing those checks does not establish remote freshness.

    Scope and limitations

    The source supplies no quantitative freshness bound or dependency protocol. WORKFLOW-GUARD-004 does not require always-latest data; ENTITY-IMPORT-007 compares expected values to the supplied observation, not to an independently queried remote system. The interview's suggestion that real-time processing removes these problems is not generalized: distributed real-time systems still require dependency and freshness policies.

  • ENTITY-IMPORT-008 - A failed Entity Import MUST NOT return a partially imported Entity, Revision, Mapping, or Conflict Version observation and MUST NOT change any existing Entity observation.
  • ENTITY-IMPORT-009 - Missing, malformed, conflicting, or incomplete identity, mapping, or revision input MUST fail with FINKORE_ENTITY_INVALID_IDENTITY unless a more specific primary domain error applies.
  • ENTITY-IMPORT-010 - Entity Import diagnostics, when supplied, MUST remain safe diagnostic context and MUST NOT expose sensitive source identity values, financial values, or implementation storage identifiers by default.
  • ENTITY-IMPORT-011 - Entity Import MUST accept complete valid Entity Identity Mapping evidence when the separate Source Identity is omitted, provided it identifies the source system, source identity, mapping identity, and the same Entity type and identity as the imported observation. It MUST preserve that evidence without synthesizing a separate Source Identity observation. Supplied null or malformed Source Identity MUST still fail under ENTITY-IMPORT-009. Omission of both Source Identity and mapping MUST remain valid when the rest of the import is valid.
  • ENTITY-IMPORT-012 - Every successful bounded Entity Import result MUST include historicalRevisions as a list. When supplied history is omitted or an empty list, the result MUST contain historicalRevisions: []. Nonempty supplied revisions MUST remain preserved under ENTITY-IMPORT-006. This output normalization MUST NOT synthesize current revisions, identity mapping, or conflict versions, alter input member presence, accept null or malformed history, change error priorities, or expose a partial result on failure. Empty history describes the supplied observation, not proof that no earlier revisions exist.

Invariants

Import observes existing Entity continuity. It preserves the stable FinKore Entity identity or records explicit continuity mapping; it does not create a global identity registry or select an Entity by searching external systems.

An imported Entity is an observed existing Entity, not a validation bypass. A validation failure uses FINKORE_ENTITY_VALIDATION_FAILED under ENTITY-VALIDATION-004 and returns no partial import observation under ENTITY-IMPORT-008.

Supplied preconditions

Supplied Source Identity is validated independently of whether mapping evidence is also present. Explicit null or another malformed supplied Source Identity is not omission and cannot be repaired by taking source values from a valid mapping. It fails with FINKORE_ENTITY_INVALID_IDENTITY under ENTITY-IMPORT-009, without a partial import under ENTITY-IMPORT-008. When both are supplied and valid, their source references agree and the mapping identifies the imported Entity under ENTITY-IMPORT-003 and ENTITY-IMPORT-005. Valid identity values remain opaque.

For the optional preconditions in ENTITY-IMPORT-007, explicit null is supplied input, not omission. Null or another malformed expected value cannot match a valid State, business revision, or conflict-version identifier; an absent observed revision/token also cannot satisfy a supplied expectation. These mismatches use FINKORE_ENTITY_STATE_CONFLICT and return no partial import under ENTITY-IMPORT-008. Malformed observed identity/revision input remains subject to ENTITY-IMPORT-009. This clarification does not introduce a total priority among unrelated Entity failures.

Standalone mapping

Under ENTITY-IMPORT-011, complete valid mapping is accepted when Source Identity is omitted, without synthesizing a separate Source Identity. Mapping remains required when Source Identity is supplied under ENTITY-IMPORT-003. Explicit null or malformed Source Identity is not omission.

Non-Goals

This document does not define concrete invoice migration, database uniqueness, merge/deduplication, source-system authentication, Workflow definition migration, state mapping across Workflow definitions, or external-system data retention policy.
